summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with type II diabetes, hypertension, and depression, was admitted for diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) due to medication noncompliance caused by inability to afford copays. She had stopped taking her insulin and glimepiride four days prior, leading to severe hyperglycemia, acidosis, and symptoms of shortness of breath and palpitations. She was treated in the ICU with an insulin drip and IV fluids, with rapid improvement in her metabolic parameters. Her anion gap closed within 24 hours, and she was transitioned to subcutaneous insulin. A mild left knee effusion was noted but not infected, and aspiration was unsuccessful. To improve adherence, her insulin regimen was changed to Humulin 70/30 twice daily, provided at no cost, and she was given new glucose monitoring supplies. She was discharged home in stable condition with clear instructions to monitor blood glucose four times daily and follow up with outpatient providers.
